summary: Configured secure one-way synchronization from node1 to node2 every minute. Changes and deletions propagated in 10–56 seconds during testing. Both nodes were restarted individually and recovered fully. The original absent-file state was restored on both nodes; OS release and kernel were unchanged.
actions_performed: Installed a root-owned sender and cron schedule on node1.
Generated a dedicated Ed25519 key and pinned node2’s SSH host key.
Installed a source-IP-restricted, forced-command receiver on node2.
Verified checksum, ownership, group, mode, deletion propagation, and rejection of arbitrary SSH commands.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot IDs and post-restart synchronization.
Removed test data and confirmed no temporary files or failed units remained.

evidence.summary: Cron runs every minute. Creation propagated with identical SHA-256 and metadata in 41 seconds; deletion propagated in 54 seconds.
The dedicated private key is mode 600; node2 restricts it by source IP and forced command; an arbitrary command was rejected with status 64.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed OS release and kernel
